profile.summary: ProSST is a protein language model that reads both a protein's amino acid sequence and its 3D structure. The structure is first converted into a sequence of discrete structure tokens, one per residue, and the model is pretrained to predict masked residues. Its main use in the repository is zero-shot prediction of the effect of amino acid substitutions, scored on the ProteinGym benchmark.
profile.summary_source_locator: Abstract; README: 4 Zero-shot mutant effect prediction

summary_quotes.text: translates a 3D protein structure into a sequence of discrete tokens by first serializing the protein structure into residue-level local structures
We pre-train ProSST on millions of protein structures using a masked language model objective

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProSST has two parts. The structure quantization module takes each residue with its 40 nearest neighbours in 3D as a local structure, embeds it with a geometric vector perceptron (GVP) encoder trained to denoise CATH structures, and assigns it to the nearest of K k-means centroids; the centroid index is the residue's structure token. A Transformer then reads the residue tokens and the structure tokens together. Its disentangled attention, adapted from DeBERTa, keeps five attention terms between residues, structure tokens and relative positions (residue-to-residue, residue-to-structure, residue-to-position, structure-to-residue and position-to-residue). The model is pretrained with structure-conditioned masked language modelling: 15% of residues are corrupted and predicted from the rest of the sequence and the uncorrupted structure tokens.

quotes.text: The structure quantization module translates a 3D protein structure into a sequence of discrete tokens by first serializing the protein structure into residue-level local structures and then embeds them into dense vector space.
These vectors are then quantized into discrete structure tokens by a pre-trained clustering model.
ProSST explicitly learns the relationship between protein residue token sequences and structure token sequences through the sequence-structure disentangled attention.
It describes the local environment of a residue by centering on a specific residue and including it along with the nearest 40 residues surrounding it in three-dimensional space
Then we apply the k-means algorithm to identify K centroids within this latent space
our sequence-structure disentangled attention mechanism includes 5 types of attention.
We randomly select 15% indices from the set M for nosing and computing loss for back-propagation.
Inspired by DeBerta [42], we use an expanded form of disentangled attention

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The checkpoints differ in the size of the structure vocabulary K (20, 128, 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096). The paper found most metrics best at K = 2048 and made it the default. The notebook and the ProteinGym command pair ProSST-2048 with structure tokens made at vocabulary size 2048. Because the checkpoints differ in K, a result should name K and the Hugging Face revision. This page read ProSST-2048 at revision e94ffee7. The repository's ProteinGym script also needs precomputed structure tokens; the README links them on Google Drive, made from the same PDB set as ProtSSN.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Protein language model that takes both the amino acid sequence and the 3D structure, pretrained with a masked language model objective.

quotes.text: a Transformer-based protein language model that seamlessly integrates both protein sequences and structures
using a masked language model objective

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: A structure quantization module (a six-layer GVP graph encoder plus a k-means codebook of K centroids) that turns a structure into discrete structure tokens, and a Transformer with sequence-structure disentangled attention. The ProSST-2048 config has 12 layers, 12 attention heads, hidden size 768, feed-forward size 3072 and relative position embeddings. The paper gives the same layers, heads and width but a feed-forward size of 3172.
facts.source_locator: config.json; paper: Section 3 and Appendix A.3

quotes.text: ProSST incorporates a structure quantization module and a Transformer architecture with disentangled attention.
The model has 12 transformer layers, 12 attention heads, and 768 embedding dims with 3172 feed-forward embedding dimensions with the GELU activation function.
The GVP encoder includes a six-layer message-passing graph neural network

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An amino acid sequence plus a sequence of structure tokens. The structure tokens are computed from a PDB file by the repository's structure quantizer, with a vocabulary of 20, 128, 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 tokens, and are shifted by 3 for special tokens before being passed to the model.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-position logits over residues from the masked language model head. The notebook scores a substitution as the log-probability of the mutant residue minus that of the wild type, summing over multiple substitutions. The paper also uses the representations for supervised downstream tasks.

quotes.text: enabling it to learn comprehensive contextual representations of proteins

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 115,589,376 (ProSST-20) to 118,719,744 (ProSST-4096), as counted by Hugging Face from the safetensors files: ProSST-20 115,589,376; ProSST-128 115,672,320; ProSST-512 115,967,232; ProSST-1024 116,360,448; ProSST-2048 117,146,880; ProSST-4096 118,719,744. The paper's Table 2 lists ProSST at 110M. The structure quantizer is a separate model; the notebook log reports 5.90M parameters for it.
facts.source_locator: Hugging Face API safetensors; paper: Table 2; notebook output

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 18.8 million AlphaFold-predicted structures: the 90% reduced version of AlphaFoldDB, with 100,000 structures held out for validation and proteins longer than 2048 residues removed. The structure encoder and codebook were trained on CATH 4.3 S40 domains (31,270 structures and 4,735,677 local structures).

quotes.text: We pre-train ProSST on millions of protein structures
We downloaded the 90% reduced version, containing 18.8 million structures.
From this collection, we randomly select 100,000 structures for validation
the dataset is reduced to 31,270 entries.
resulting in 4,735,677 local structures from the protein structures in CATH43-S40.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Six main checkpoints on Hugging Face, one per structure vocabulary size: AI4Protein/ProSST-20, -128, -512, -1024, -2048 and -4096. The README uses ProSST-2048 in its examples. The AI4Protein organisation also lists ProSST-Foldseek, ProSST-DSSP, four ProSST-NO_* models and three ProSSTX-2048 models, which the README does not describe.
facts.source_locator: README: 2 and 3; Hugging Face API responses

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not stated. The paper names the AlphaFoldDB 90% reduced set and CATH 4.3 but gives no download date.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 2048 residues: proteins longer than 2048 residues were removed from pretraining. Relative positions are clipped at 1024 (max_relative_positions 1024 in the ProSST-2048 config, matching the paper's Lmax). The paper states no maximum length for inference.

quotes.text: During pre-training, proteins with more than 2048 resiudes (594 samples) are removed for training efficacy.
Lmax represents the maximum relative distance we consider, which is set to 1024 in the implementation.

facts.value: Code: https://github.com/ai4protein/ProSST. Weights: https://huggingface.co/AI4Protein/ProSST-2048 and the other AI4Protein/ProSST-* repositories, none gated. Quantized ProteinGym structures are on Google Drive, linked from the README.

strengths.text: Uses structure as well as sequence: the structure enters as discrete per-residue tokens computed directly from a PDB file.

quotes.text: These tokens serve as an effective protein structure representation.

strengths.text: Weights load through Hugging Face transformers, and the repository includes a script that runs the full ProteinGym substitution benchmark.
The authors report state-of-the-art zero-shot mutation effect prediction among their baselines; this is the authors' claim.

quotes.text: we conduct extensive experiments on the zero-shot mutation effect prediction and several supervised downstream tasks, where ProSST achieves the state-of-the-art performance among all baselines

limitations.text: Needs a 3D structure for each protein, converted to structure tokens before scoring. For proteins without one, the authors suggest predicting a structure with AlphaFold2 or ESMFold; with ESMFold structures their ProteinGym score fell from 0.504 to 0.471. They also report that the structure quantization needs heavy computation and that performance drops for proteins with low AlphaFold confidence.
limitations.source_locator: README; paper: Section 5, Appendices A.6 and A.7

quotes.text: the local structure construction and encoding requires heavy computations.
These results suggest that structure-aware models may exhibit limitations in accurately predicting the structures of disordered proteins.

limitations.text: The repository is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: no commercial use and no distribution of modified code. The weights carry no licence of their own on Hugging Face.

Loading the weights runs custom model code from the Hugging Face repository (trust_remote_code=True), and the ProSST-2048 model card is the unfilled Hugging Face template, so details on training data and intended use come only from the paper.

The ProSST-2048 model card is an empty template and declares no licence; the other cards were not read.

The paper reports pretraining on one 8 x 80G A800 server for about a month. Hardware needs for inference are given only as a speed plot on a 3090 GPU, with no figures in the text. The requirements file pins CUDA 11.8 builds of PyTorch Geometric packages.
The paper describes a ProSST (MST) variant that accepts sequence-only input; the files read do not show which, if any, Hugging Face checkpoint it is.
The other ProSST variants on Hugging Face (Foldseek, DSSP, ablations, ProSSTX) were not reviewed.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository at a pinned commit, turn a PDB file into structure tokens, and score substitutions on one protein with ProSST-2048.
prerequisites: Python with pip. requirements.txt pins torch==2.1.1 and transformers==4.38.2, and CUDA 11.8 builds of torch-scatter, torch-sparse and related packages. GPU type and memory are not stated.
A protein structure as a PDB file.
Code is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use only. The weights are not gated.

python - <<'PY'
from prosst.structure.get_sst_seq import SSTPredictor
predictor = SSTPredictor(structure_vocab_size=2048) # can be 20, 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096
result = predictor.predict_from_pdb('example_data/p1.pdb')
print(result)

steps.explanation: The README snippet wrapped in a shell heredoc, with a print line added. It quantizes the example structure in the repository into structure tokens.

steps.title: Score mutants on one protein
steps.shell:
cd zero_shot
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer
from prosst.structure.get_sst_seq import SSTPredictor
from Bio import SeqIO
import torch
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

prosst_model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("AI4Protein/ProSST-2048", trust_remote_code=True)
prosst_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("AI4Protein/ProSST-2048", trust_remote_code=True)
predictor = SSTPredictor(structure_vocab_size=2048)

residue_sequence = str(SeqIO.read('example_data/GRB2_HUMAN_Faure_2021.fasta', 'fasta').seq)
structure_sequence = predictor.predict_from_pdb("example_data/GRB2_HUMAN_Faure_2021.pdb")[0]['2048_sst_seq']
structure_sequence_offset = [i + 3 for i in structure_sequence]

tokenized_res = prosst_tokenizer([residue_sequence], return_tensors='pt')
input_ids = tokenized_res['input_ids']
attention_mask = tokenized_res['attention_mask']
structure_input_ids = torch.tensor([1, *structure_sequence_offset, 2], dtype=torch.long).unsqueeze(0)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = prosst_model(
        input_ids=input_ids,
        attention_mask=attention_mask,
        ss_input_ids=structure_input_ids
    )
logits = torch.log_softmax(outputs.logits[:, 1:-1], dim=-1).squeeze()

df = pd.read_csv("example_data/GRB2_HUMAN_Faure_2021.csv")
mutants = df['mutant'].tolist()
vocab = prosst_tokenizer.get_vocab()
pred_scores = []
for mutant in mutants:
    mutant_score = 0
    for sub_mutant in mutant.split(":"):
        wt, idx, mt = sub_mutant[0], int(sub_mutant[1:-1]) - 1, sub_mutant[-1]
        pred = logits[idx, vocab[mt]] - logits[idx, vocab[wt]]
        mutant_score += pred.item()
    pred_scores.append(mutant_score)

print(spearmanr(pred_scores, df['DMS_score']))
PY
steps.explanation: The code cells of zero_shot/score_mutant.ipynb joined into one shell heredoc, run from the zero_shot directory (the notebook does sys.path.append('..'), and its example_data paths resolve there). Step 3 prints the Spearman correlation between the predicted mutant scores and the DMS scores; the notebook's saved output for GRB2 is SignificanceResult(statistic=0.7182950462783597, pvalue=0.0).

notes: ProteinGym reports six ProSST columns (K=20, 128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096); this record is the family, and the input locator names K=20. released is the date the host records for the weights (the Hugging Face createdAt field: 2024-05-15 for most checkpoints, 2024-07-04 for ProSST-2048), the same rule used for the other models in this batch; it is an upload date, not necessarily the training date. The bioRxiv v1 page is titled DeProt, an earlier name for the same preprint; it was not used as a source. Its text layer has no IP address stamp; it carries author email addresses, not copied to the page.
